title: Affine sections of a coherent formal system form an adic module tower
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], I an ideal, X=Spec A [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and J the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf associated with I. For a coherent formal J-module F [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], put T_n=Gamma(X,F_n), as an A-module via the global sections isomorphism Gamma(X,O_X)=A [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. Index n denotes level n+1. Every T_n is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], I^(n+1)T_n=0, and the successor transition T_(n+1) -> T_n is surjective with kernel I^(n+1)T_(n+1). This statement concerns only sections of finite-level sheaves, not an inverse limit.

proof.text: Spec A is locally Noetherian. Apply isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType to each F_n. Reuse the proved finite_sections_of_finiteType helper from QuasicoherentFiniteTypeAffine via a proof-only import all to obtain finite global sections over Gamma(Spec A,O). Apply finite_sections_top_of_finite to transport finiteness to A.

The ideal-times-quasi-coherent affine theorem gives quasi-coherence of positive sheaf powers and identifies the range of their inclusions with J(U)^(n+1). Reuse its proved multiplication_range and product_qc helpers via a proof-only import all: the powered inclusion multiplied by M has range J(U)^(n+1) times M(U), and its product object is quasi-coherent. The quasi-coherent cokernel/image theorem gives surjectivity of the quotient projection and identifies its kernel with that product range. At level n the formal-system zero-product condition makes the inclusion zero, so the calculated range is zero.

On the top affine open, hJ and ideal_top_ofIdealTop identify J(U) with the extension of I along GammaSpecIso.inv. Ideal.map_pow and Submodule.restrictScalars_map_smul_eq identify the product submodule after restricting scalars with I^(n+1) times the A-section module; smul_top_eq verifies the scalar tower. Apply sections to the defining quotient isomorphism e. Its linear equivalence is surjective and sends a section to zero exactly when the section is zero. Rewrite the transition by quotientProjection composed with e; combine quotient surjectivity and the calculated kernel to obtain both transition conclusions.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_affine_sections_adic (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (J : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom))
    (F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) :
    let T := F.obj ⋙ moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A)
    (∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite A (T.obj (op n))) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op n))) = ⊥) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ∧
      LinearMap.ker (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom =
        I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op (n + 1)))))
